title: Prevent regressions in Zedu’s core learning workflows
description: Create repeatable automated checks for signing in, joining a workspace, inviting a member, using channels and threads, sharing a file, and starting or joining a Buzz call. Reuse the approved test workspace and synthetic data only. Done when the checks can run before each release, produce clear pass/fail evidence, cover important recovery paths, and state who responds when a check fails. Public-page SEO checks are out of scope.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Add poor-network and reconnect cases to the release checks
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The accepted suite covers the six main workflows and recovery from errors, but it does not define what should happen when connectivity drops or becomes very slow. In the approved synthetic test workspace, add reproducible checks for an interrupted file upload, a dropped Buzz connection and an invite link opened after a temporary network failure. For each, record expected state, retry or recovery path, and evidence; use throttling/stubs only where they model the behavior reliably, and label real-network limits as untested. Fold the cases into the existing release gate rather than creating another test runner. Do not claim low-data support unless the product verifies it.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Build on the Cypress suite zedu-fe already has: add the missing workflows, a headless run and a release gate
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
Checked on 22 Oct 2026 in zedu-fe cybertron-integration at 214cb29. The repo already has Cypress 13 with 22 spec files and 43 tests (auth, profile, messaging attachments, two Buzz specs, search, marketing). But: 1) no CI workflow runs them (0 of the 29 files in .github/workflows mention cypress, e2e or playwright), and the only script is 'cypress open', which is interactive, so nothing produces pass or fail evidence before a release. 2) Of the goal's six workflows, sign-in is covered (login, logout, sign-up, forgot and reset password), file sharing is partly covered (messaging/attachments.cy.ts), the two Buzz specs check host name and live duration but do not start or join a call, and I found no spec for joining a workspace, inviting a member, or channels and threads. 3) Some specs still use the old product name (test_telex_homepage, test_talex_blogpage, test_telex_faqpage), so some may be stale; a failed-run screenshot is committed in cypress/screenshots.

Approach: 1) Baseline: run the existing 22 specs headless against the approved test workspace and record which pass, fail or are stale. 2) Write a coverage table for the six workflows (covered, partial, missing) from that run. 3) Add the missing specs using synthetic data only, each with its recovery path (wrong password, expired or reused invite, failed upload, microphone denied on a Buzz call). 4) Add a 'cypress run' script and a pre-release CI job that saves the video and screenshots as the pass or fail evidence. 5) Add a one-page owner table: for each check, who responds when it fails and by when. Tasks: baseline run and coverage table (research), missing specs with paste-ready code (seo is wrong here: use content or other), CI job and owner table (other).

Limits: I have not run the suite, and a run needs the approved test workspace credentials, which belong in the git-ignored cypress.env.json (there is a sample.cypress.env.json); I would not hold or print them.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Define the pass/fail contract per workflow first: expected states, recovery paths and who responds when a check fails
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The accepted workstream builds the automated checks; this idea defines what a pass actually means, so the evidence is comparable release to release. For each of the six workflows (signing in, joining a workspace, inviting a member, channels and threads, sharing a file, starting or joining a Buzz call): 1) write the exact expected state at every step, using the approved test workspace and synthetic data only; 2) name the failure modes that matter (for example an invite landing in the wrong workspace, a Buzz link joining as a guest, a shared file unreadable by the recipient); 3) state the recovery path each check must verify; 4) name the human who responds when that check fails. Deliver a one-page contract per workflow plus a release-gate run sheet: which checks must be green before a release, how pass/fail evidence is attached, and the escalation order. Done when: every automated check can be traced to a stated expected behavior, every failure has a recovery path and a named responder, and the run sheet can be executed by someone new. Measured: six contracts, six recovery paths, six named responders; a release can only be blocked by a failed check with a recorded reason. Public-page SEO checks stay out of scope. Why this fits: it complements the Cypress workstream instead of duplicating it - the tests will assert the contract this idea defines, and the goal's 'who responds when a check fails' question gets a real answer.
